player.seasonOutlook: Wembanyama made a leap in Year 3 as arguably the most impactful player in the NBA. On the fantasy front, he set new career highs in scoring (25.0 PPG), rebounds (11.5 RPG) and field goal percentage (51.2%). He took a step back in both blocks (3.1 BPG) and 3-pointers (1.9 3PG), but he still led the league in blocks by a large margin and was top-5 among centers in treys. Wembanyama has missed 54 games over the last two seasons, so durability is a concern, but otherwise he projects as potentially the top producer in category leagues.

Jokic has been the top fantasy points scorer for six seasons and counting. He is coming off his second straight season averaging a triple-double, in which he notched a career-best 10.7 APG. The Nuggets offense is built entirely around Jokic, and he is surrounded by finishers at every position, which helps him generate assists and also opens up space for his own scoring. Jokic also remains one of the best rebounders in the league. Barring injury, he projects to lead the league in fantasy points yet again this season.

Gilgeous-Alexander won his second straight NBA MVP last season and remains one of the most consistent fantasy producers in the league. The Thunder are built perfectly to accentuate his strengths, with finishers and 3-and-D shooters at every position. This provides space for SGA to create off the dribble to generate efficient looks, assist opportunities and free throws galore. He has also averaged almost 72 games per season for the last four campaigns, making him a reliable high-production option.

Maxey is coming off a campaign in which he averaged career highs in all six fantasy counting categories: points, assists, rebounds, steals, 3-pointers and blocks. He was fifth in fantasy points per game and fourth in total fantasy points and is still only 25 years old. The 76ers made big moves this offseason, bringing in both Jaylen Brown and LeBron James. While this increases the team's chances to contend, it likely puts a cap on Maxey's volume upside.

Doncic has won the NBA scoring crown in two of the last three seasons: his last full season with the Mavericks and his first full season with the Lakers. With former teammate LeBron James no longer on the squad, Doncic appears poised for the biggest season of his career. He has massive usage in the Lakers' offense, a talented second option in Austin Reaves to take some defensive pressure off, and finishers at every other position. The main risk is health, with Doncic having missed 50 games over the last two seasons, but when healthy he should challenge for top fantasy scorer in the league.

Mitchell has consistently been one of the most productive guards in fantasy, and last season was no exception. The Cavaliers made a big in-season trade, sending out Darius Garland and bringing back James Harden, but Mitchell's numbers remained largely consistent in 22 games next to Harden. Harden is a higher usage point guard than Garland but is also a better distributor which should ultimately lead to better looks for Mitchell. Mitchell's shot volume upside may be slightly capped but his efficiency improvement could be even more impactful.

Antetokounmpo ended his storied career with the Bucks this offseason and will begin a new chapter with the Heat. Antetokounmpo has been one of the most consistent producers in fantasy this generation; in the seven seasons leading up to last, he averaged a rounded 30 points, 11 rebounds and 6 assists per game. Injuries limited him to only 36 games in 2025-26, but if he stays healthy Antetkounmpo should bounce back to his typical production this season.

Cunningham set career highs in assists (9.9 APG), steals (1.4 SPG) and blocks (0.8 BPG) last season while turning in the sixth-best fantasy scoring average in the league. Entering his sixth season, Cunningham looks to take another step forward as the team leader for the Pistons and a budding MVP candidate. Cunningham has only played more than 64 games in one season of his career, so durability is of concern, but he has averaged 67 games in his last two seasons ... the best two-season stretch of his career.

Durant enters his 20th NBA season as still one of the best scorers in the league. Standing near 7-foot with one of the smoothest jumpers in NBA history, Durant has a playing style that remains effective regardless of age. He is the elder statesman on a talented Rockets team that will get starting point guard Fred VanVleet back this season. Playing with VanVleet should get Durant better looks in the halfcourt offense, so health-willing he could replicate or even surpass his production last season when he ranked 15th in the league in fantasy scoring.

Flagg is coming off a Rookie of the Year campaign but has the potential for major improvements in Year 2. Last season, then-head coach Jason Kidd experimented with Flagg at point guard, an added level of difficulty for a rookie already making the transition to the highest level. This season, new coach Dusty May and returning point guard Kyrie Irving should put Flagg in more advantageous positions to attack defenses. His stats should increase across the board, giving him fantasy upside as high as top-10.

Towns modified his game last season to fit in with his strong Knicks teammates, turning in his lowest scoring average (20.1 PPG) since his rookie season with his fewest 3-pointers (1.5 3PG) since 2018-19. On the positive side, Towns still has averaged more than 20 PPG in 10 straight seasons and has posted 12.4 RPG in his two seasons with the Knicks, his best marks since 2018-19. Towns also emerged in the playoffs as a strong passer that can generate big assist numbers, should the team decide to run more offense through him.

Tatum missed most of last season but was able to return for the last 16 games. His production was understandably limited, but it was important that he got those games under his belt before resuming his role as the franchise player for the Celtics this season. Tatum will likely assume an even larger role after Jaylen Brown was traded this offseason, and with increased usage he has the chance to turn in his most productive fantasy season if health allows.

Booker is one of the most consistent players in the NBA. His per-game averages last season were all within decimal points of his averages across the last eight seasons. While his star teammates and supporting cast change, Booker's numbers remain largely the same year-to-year. This should be the case again this season, with games played as the largest variable. In that eight year span, Booker has played as many as 77 games and as few as 53.

Brunson reached the pinnacle of the NBA last season by leading the Knicks to their first championship in more than 50 years. He also turned in another strong fantasy campaign, almost exactly in line with his four year averages of a rounded 26 PPG, 3 RPG and 7 APG. The Knicks have one of the more stable lineups in the league, returning the same starting crew with similar roles. Brunson is still squarely in his prime at 30 years old, and his expectations this season should remain right in line with what he has done since arriving in New York.

Brown is coming off his best individual season, operating as the sole focal point of the Celtics' offense with Jayson Tatum sidelined. After being traded to the 76ers this offseason, he is now in the opposite situation with several other high-usage teammates to share the ball with. Brown is in his peak seasons so should play well even with fewer shots, but his shot volume should lower significantly playing next to Tyrese Maxey, LeBron James, Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe.

Barnes has been a metronome of consistency for the past three seasons, averaging a rounded 19 points, 8 rebounds, 6 assists and 3 combined blocks and steals on a year-in, year-out basis. His Raptors made a major move this offseason in bringing back Kawhi Leonard in exchange for Brandon Ingram. Barnes' role should remain similar but his volume and efficiency could actually increase a bit, with similar usage against softer defenses more focused on stopping Leonard.

Curry played only 43 games last season, and reportedly there are concerns about the long-term health of his knee going into this season. Entering his 18th season at age 38, durability and availability are legitimate concerns for Curry. He is still an elite producer when he's on the court, but it is risky to draft him early in fantasy leagues.

After playing his first six seasons with the Hornets, Ball was traded this offseason to the Timberwolves. Ball, the No. 3 overall pick in the 2020 NBA draft will be joining Anthony Edwards, the No. 1 overall pick in the same draft, to form one of the most explosive backcourts in the NBA. Ball is a brilliant, creative offensive talent whose passes and long-range shot attempts often look haphazard even as they prove effective. The biggest question mark is availability; last season was one of only two in Ball's career in which he was able to play more than 51 games.

Injuries limited Davis to only 20 games last season and only 29 total with the Mavericks since his midseason trade there in the 2024-25 season. Last season, Davis was traded again to the Wizards though he was never able to play. This season, Davis is expected to return healthy and settle in as the primary big man for the Wizards. He will play next to point guard Trae Young, who excels at running the pick-and-roll and setting up his big man with easy shots. Durability is always a concern for Davis, but if he can remain healthy he could be in for the most efficient scoring season of his career playing next to Young.

Sabonis' season was cut short by a knee injury that limited him to only 19 games, by far the fewest in a campaign in his career. In his three previous full seasons with the Kings, Sabonis had averaged a rounded 19 points, 13 rebounds and 7 assists in 77 games per year. The Kings have signaled a rebuild, letting veterans like DeMar DeRozan walk, and there are rumors that Sabonis could be on the move as well, but as long as he remains in Sacramento expect Sabonis to bounce back to his typical usage levels this season.

Harden was traded to the Cavaliers midseason in exchange for Darius Garland, forming a dynamic backcourt with Donovan Mitchell. Pairing with Mitchell caps Harden's volume. and Harden's usage dropped dramatically after the trade in 26 games last season. In fact, it fell to a value that would have represented the second-lowest season-long Usage percentage over a full season since 2012. Expect his fantasy value this season to be lower than his norm, but even attenuated he remains an impact fantasy starter.

After spending his first seven seasons with the Atlanta Hawks, Young was traded to the Wizards in January. Young battled injury before and after the trade and was limited to only 15 total games played, the fewest in his career. This season, Young will be the leader of a new-look Wizards squad featuring fellow All-Star Anthony Davis and rookie No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa. Young will be surrounded by finishers and potential pick-and-roll partners, which bodes well for a player in Young who increased his assists per game in each of his first seven seasons in the league.

Murray played 75 games last season, his highest numbers since the 2018-19 season. He reached a new peak in his ninth season, establishing career highs of 25.4 PPG, 7.1 APG and 4.4 RPG. Those numbers are similar to Murray's typical playoffs averages, but this was the first time he performed at that level in the regular season. Murray has perfected the art of playing off Nikola Jokic, and as long as his health allows he should be in line for similar or better production in this campaign.

James willingly accepted a third option role with the Lakers last season, allowing Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves to operate at higher usage. After signing with the 76ers this offseason, James finds himself in a similar situation where he will likely be the third or fourth option behind teammates Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid. James may play some point forward, so his assists may increase, but his scoring volume and overall fantasy production are likely capped.

Reaves made a star leap last season, proving that he had the capacity to produce major numbers when given the opportunity to. With LeBron James no longer on the Lakers' roster, Reaves now slots as the full-time second option on the team behind Luka Doncic with major upside whenever Doncic is out of the lineup. In four games when both Doncic and James were out of the lineup last season, Reaves averaged a whopping 39.0 PPG and 9.5 APG.

Sengun is one of the best combinations of post scoring and passing in the NBA; in the last three seasons he has averaged a rounded 20 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists per game with a block and a steal to boot. Sengun has remained a primary scoring option even on a team featuring Kevin Durant, and at only 24 years old he should continue to develop into one of the franchise cornerstones on a talented Rockets roster. Last season, he ranked 14th in the NBA in fantasy points per game.

Adebayo has been very consistent with his production, and last year was no exception. In the last four years, Adebayo has averaged a rounded 20 points and 10 rebounds while playing about 74 games per year, and last season his averages were within decimal points of his four-year mark in every major category except field goal percentage (down) and 3-pointers (up significantly). Both of those should be helped by the presence of new teammate Giannis Antetokounmpo, who demands defensive help and should open up easier shots for the veteran Adebayo.

Johnson has increased his scoring, rebounding and assists in each of his five seasons up to last season's rounded 23 points, 10 rebounds and 8 assists. He stepped forward as the franchise player for the Hawks, particularly after they traded away Trae Young. Johnson moves into this season as one of the few players in the league that has legitimate upside to average a triple-double.

Mobley only played 65 games last season due to injury, the third time in his five seasons that he has played less than 70 games. His production largely stayed consistent with the season before, within decimal points of 18 points, 9 rebounds, 3 assists, 2 blocks and 1 steal in both campaigns. At 25 years old, Mobley should still be improving year-over-year, so durability will be the biggest factor in his fantasy potential this season.

Thompson was drafted as a once-a-generation athlete with the skill to potentially develop into a lead guard on offense and an elite defensive wing on defense. He has developed rapidly, improving his scoring, rebounding, and assist and steal numbers in each of his first three seasons. Thompson will likely step back as a distributor this season with the return of starting point guard Fred VanVleet, but that should come with a corresponding increase in scoring opportunities with better looks. Still only 23 years old, Thompson should continue to make significant improvements in 2026-27.

Edwards set new career bests in scoring (28.8 PPG) and field goal percentage (48.9 FG%) last season and could be set to improve on both marks this season after the Timberwolves traded for point guard LaMelo Ball. Edwards has never played next to an offense creator and facilitator of Ball's caliber, so he should get better looks and easier opportunities this season than he's ever had. Edwards has clear 30+ PPG upside and should again be among the league leaders in 3-pointers made.

Siakam had the second-biggest scoring season of his career in 2025-26 as he tried to pick up the offensive slack with Tyrese Haliburton injured. This might suggest that Haliburton's return could eat into Siakam's numbers, but Siakam has now had more than two seasons to acclimate to the Pacers and establish himself as a franchise cornerstone. With the return of Haliburton's distribution skills putting him in better positions to score, Siakam may retain his elevated scoring this season.

Haliburton is returning after a year away from the NBA recovering from a torn Achilles tendon. In his three full seasons with the Pacers, Haliburton has averaged a rounded 20-10 points-assists double-double with good shooting percentages and almost three 3-pointers a night. While Haliburton may be monitored early in the season, he is more than a year removed from the injury and expected to return to his typical level before long. The Pacers have shooters and finishers at every position, so if he is at full strength Haliburton has the potential to challenge for the league lead in assists.

Avdija exploded last season, far surpassing his previous career best marks in scoring (24.2 PPG) and assists (6.7 APG) as he grew into the franchise player for the Trail Blazers. Avdija spent large swathes of the season as a point forward with nightly triple-double upside, but once Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson were healthy Avdija became more of a finisher. He is likely to lean even more into the finisher role this season, with the Trail Blazers fielding at least four starting caliber point guards to fill the floor general slots.

Porter thrived in his first season with the Nets, leaning into the lead role to increase his scoring career high by more than five points up to the mid-20s. Porter remains the main option this season even after the trade that brought Julius Randle to town and should continue to produce. The question with Porter is always durability: he has only played more than 62 games twice in his seven-year career.

At 28 years old, Fox finds himself as the grizzled veteran on a team full of young, up-and-coming superstars. Fox's scoring in his first full season with the Spurs (18.6 PPG) was more than six points lower than his average for the five previous seasons (24.7 PPG), in large part because he had to share shots with Victor Wembanyama and Stephon Castle. Also because he had to share minutes with Dylan Harper, who played well as a rookie and seems poised to pop as a sophomore. Fox's minutes and production could go down more this season as the three young stars all take on even larger roles.

Williamson played 62 games last season, a positive bounce-back from the 30 he played the season before, and the second-most games he has played in the eight seasons since he was drafted. Williamson also had his smallest role with the Pelicans last season, notching career-lows in both points and rebounds per game. The Pelicans have a lot of startable talent in their frontcourt, including young players they want to build around, so Williamson's role and future with the Pelicans have enough questions to limit his fantasy upside even beyond the availability concerns.

Availability is the primary question when it comes to Embiid's fantasy prospects. His production is still elite when he is on the court, but in the last two seasons he has only played in 57 of a possible 164 games. His durability history makes him difficult to draft before the middle-late rounds of fantasy drafts, but if this were the season where he could play even 60 games Embiid could be a league-winning player. The 76ers are chock full of talent with the offseason additions of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, but when the 32-year-old Embiid is on the court he still defaults to a primary role in the team's offense.

Castle increased his role and production in Year 2, up from his Rookie of the Year numbers from the season before. He was drafted as an elite defender with the size to guard wings and the speed to guard point guards, but his offense took a big leap as well. He increased his scoring average and almost doubled his assist output. When healthy, the Spurs have two other strong lead guards in De'Aaron Fox and Dylan Harper that may cap Castle's assist opportunities, but he has room to increase his scoring and has 20 PPG potential in Year 3.

Irving missed all of last season with a torn ACL but is reportedly almost fully recovered. He rejoins a very different Mavericks team, with Cooper Flagg as the new centerpiece and both Luka Doncic and Anthony Davis traded away. Irving is a high-usage guard that adjusted his passing game to play with Doncic; he should have the chance to create more offense and thus better fantasy numbers as the lead guard next to Flagg.
